title: Color Emotions for Multi-Colored Images

findings.antecedent: Color content of multicolored images (RGB histogram decomposition into activity, weight, heat factors)
findings.consequent: Observer emotional judgments on activity, weight, heat scales
findings.statement: Pearson correlation coefficient between predicted emotion values and observer judgments for heat factor is 0.97 (mean positions) and 0.90 (all positions)
findings.quote: Heat and weight resulted in correlation coefficients as high as 0.97 and 0.98
findings.scope_conditions: Multicolored images from database (5000+ images); interval scaling method with observers judging emotion placement on ruler
findings.stimulus_description: 30 multicolored images randomly selected from 5000-image database; displayed on web interface with emotion ruler scales (cool-warm, heavy-light, passive-active)
findings.mechanism: Color histogram decomposition into three emotion factors (activity, weight, heat) derived from psychophysical experiments on single colors; factors computed from RGB values transformed to CIELAB color space
theory_links: Ou et al. (2004) color emotion models for single colors and two-color combinations
Sato et al. color emotion framework
Quinean coherentist approach: color emotions are coherent across single colors and multicolored images

findings.antecedent: Color content of multicolored images (RGB histogram decomposition into weight factor)
findings.consequent: Observer emotional judgments on weight scale (heavy-light)
findings.statement: Pearson correlation coefficient between predicted weight values and observer judgments is 0.98 (mean positions) and 0.93 (all positions)

instruments_used.name: RGB histogram analysis
instruments_used.construct_measured: weight factor derived from CIELAB lightness

findings.scope_conditions: Main study with 30 multicolored images; interval scaling method with 33 observers
findings.stimulus_description: 30 multicolored images selected from 5000-image database using stratified sampling (10 samples per emotion category across activity, weight, heat scales)
findings.mechanism: Weight factor computed from histogram of CIELAB lightness values (L*) across image pixels; formula: weight = -1.8 + 0.04(100 - L*) + 0.45 cos(h - 100°)
theory_links: Lightness (L*) and chroma (C*) are most important factors in color emotions (supported by cross-cultural research)

findings.antecedent: Color content of multicolored images (RGB histogram decomposition into activity factor)
findings.consequent: Observer emotional judgments on activity scale (passive-active)
findings.statement: Pearson correlation coefficient between predicted activity values and observer judgments is 0.86 (mean positions) and 0.68 (all positions)

instruments_used.name: RGB histogram analysis
instruments_used.construct_measured: activity factor derived from CIELAB chroma

findings.scope_conditions: Main study with 30 multicolored images; activity factor is harder for observers to comprehend and apply
findings.stimulus_description: 30 multicolored images with emotion vectors plotted in 3D emotion space
findings.mechanism: Activity factor computed from saturation and hue of CIELAB values; formula involves chroma (C*) and hue angle (h); activity is more abstract and less visually obvious than weight
theory_links: Activity factor is harder for observers to understand than heat and weight factors (weaker correlation reflects this)

findings.antecedent: Observer ratings for different emotion factors (heat, weight, activity)
findings.consequent: Interobserver agreement measured by normalized root mean square error (NRMS)
findings.statement: Interobserver agreement obtained for NRMS: 0.099 for heat, 0.079 for weight, 0.160 for activity
findings.quote: Interobserver agreement obtained are 0.099 for the heat factor, 0.079 for weight, and 0.160 for activity
findings.scope_conditions: Main study; 33 observers; interval scaling method; lower NRMS indicates better agreement
findings.stimulus_description: 30 multicolored images displayed on web interface with emotion rulers
findings.mechanism: NRMS calculated as RMS / (x_max - x_min) where RMS is root mean square error between each observer and mean; normalizes agreement by scale range
theory_links: Better interobserver agreement for heat and weight compared to activity suggests these factors are more intuitive to observers

findings.consequent: Relationship between NRMS and correlation coefficient
findings.statement: Lower interobserver correlation (r) correlates with higher interobserver agreement (NRMS), indicating that poorer interobserver agreement has negative influence on correlation. NRMS values inversely related to correlation coefficients across heat, weight, activity factors
findings.quote: A poorer interobserver agreement for activity factor has a negative influence on the correlation
findings.scope_conditions: Comparison across three emotion factors; reveals that activity factor shows both lower agreement and lower correlation
findings.mechanism: When observers disagree more on specific samples (high NRMS for that sample), the correlation between predicted and actual values is reduced because the actual mean becomes less reliable
theory_links: Measurement reliability constrains validity of predictive models

findings.antecedent: Intra-sample agreement across multiple samples (1-10) for each emotion factor
findings.consequent: Consistency of observer judgments within samples
findings.statement: Mean intra-sample agreement NRMS values: 0.10 for heat, 0.08 for weight, and 0.17 for activity; agreement is stronger within samples than between samples, confirming that representativeness of image selection is critical
findings.source: Page 219, Application in Image Retrieval section; Figure 8
findings.quote: The mean intra-sample agreements are 0.10 for heat, 0.08 for weight, and 0.17 for activity
findings.scope_conditions: 10 samples for each emotion factor selected during main study
findings.stimulus_description: 10 samples from the main study emotion factor sets
findings.mechanism: Samples selected from emotion space to represent different regions; intra-sample agreement measured to assess whether images with same sample number have similar emotional properties
theory_links: Sample selection strategy affects both the coverage of emotion space and the reliability of observer judgments

findings.antecedent: Pilot study observer ratings (52 observers) for multicolored images
findings.consequent: Main study sample selection and observer count
findings.statement: 52 observers participated in pilot study judging 5000+ randomly selected images. The results from pilot study informed the main study design, including selection of 30 representative images and reduction of observer count to 33 to improve reliability while maintaining validity
findings.quote: Totally 52 observers participated in the study, judging in total 367 samples
findings.scope_conditions: Pilot study; observers recruited from public web page
findings.stimulus_description: Random samples from 5000-image database; 5-point category scales for each emotion factor
findings.mechanism: Pilot study tested simplicity of interface and visual discriminability of emotion samples; results led to main study refinements
theory_links: Iterative design approach (Engeldrüm) used to refine measurement instrument

findings.antecedent: Emotion-based image retrieval using L2 norm distance in emotion space
findings.consequent: Successful image retrieval from database based on query emotion words
findings.statement: Emotion-based retrieval method successfully retrieves images from 249,587-image database using color emotion descriptors; five best matches shown for sample queries with emotion words (cool, warm, heavy, light, passive, active)

sample.population: multicolored images from internet search engine

instruments_used.name: L2 norm distance metric
instruments_used.construct_measured: similarity between query and database images in emotion space

findings.source: Page 219-220, Application in Image Retrieval section; Figure 10
findings.quote: The five best matches for each query are shown
findings.scope_conditions: Large-scale internet image database (249,587 images); emotion space divided into 64 leaves using balanced tree with 8 entries per leaf
findings.stimulus_description: Sample query emotion descriptors: active-passive, heavy-light, warm-cool; each query retrieves images with nearest emotion vectors in L2 norm
findings.mechanism: Images described by emotion histograms derived from RGB color content; user specifies query emotion word via slider; system retrieves images with emotion vectors nearest to query in L2 norm using balanced tree index structure
theory_links: Content-based image retrieval using semantic emotion properties enables search engines unavailable with traditional keyword approaches

findings.antecedent: Observer familiarity and viewing environment conditions (illumination, background, monitor settings)
findings.consequent: Emotional response variability and model applicability in uncontrolled environments
findings.statement: Results from controlled laboratory conditions may not generalize to uncontrolled internet environments where viewing conditions vary significantly. Unknown viewing environment, illumination, background, and monitor settings may affect emotional responses and influence results. Activity factor is particularly difficult for observers unfamiliar with large emotion scale range

sample.population: Hypothetical users of emotion-based image retrieval system

findings.quote: Unknown viewing environment, like illumination settings, background colors, etc. may vary significantly, and affect the user's emotional response
findings.stimulus_description: Multicolored images viewed in variable environmental conditions
findings.mechanism: Perceptual and cognitive factors (context, familiarity, cultural background) moderate emotional responses to colors; uncontrolled conditions introduce noise and confounds
theory_links: Color emotion research typically conducted in controlled laboratory conditions; generalization to real-world viewing environments uncertain
findings.moderators_reported: Viewing environment (illumination, background, monitor settings), observer familiarity with emotion scale

limitations: Study conducted on public web page with unknown observer environment conditions (illumination, background, monitor settings) affecting emotional responses

Activity factor harder for observers to comprehend and apply than heat and weight factors, resulting in weaker correlation (0.86 vs. 0.97-0.98) and higher intra-sample agreement NRMS (0.17 vs. 0.08-0.10)
No visual distinction possible between images with poor intra-sample agreement, limiting ability to improve measurement through statistical analysis alone
Interval scaling method involves arbitrary constants (multiplier, additive constant) that may not fully capture observer judgment scaling, though Engeldrum normalization procedure applied
Generalization to uncontrolled environments uncertain; color emotions may be influenced by different regional and cultural backgrounds
Method uses content-based color analysis only; actual image content (objects, faces) also affects emotional response but not modeled in this approach
RGB space unevenly spaced in emotion space; method assumes RGB histogram adequately represents emotional color content
overall_theory_links: Ou et al. (2004) color emotion models for single colors and two-color combinations extended to multicolored images
Predictive model successfully extends single-color and two-color emotion frameworks (Ou et al., Sato et al.) to multicolored image retrieval
Support for coherentist epistemology: color emotions consistent across different color complexities (single colors, two-color combinations, multicolored images)
Three emotion factors (activity, weight, heat) derived from psychophysical experiments; heat and weight are lightness and chroma related, more salient than hue
Cross-cultural and temporal stability of color emotions (Gao et al., Xin et al., Beke et al.) supports use in image retrieval systems
RGB histogram decomposition into CIELAB coordinates enables efficient computational extraction of emotional color content for large-scale image databases

notes_on_extraction.article_structure: Introduction → Related Work → Limitations → Predictive Model → Psychophysical Experiments (Pilot and Main Study) → Results and Discussions → Application in Image Retrieval → Conclusions → References
empirical_components: Pilot study: 52 observers rating 5000+ images on 5-point emotion category scales
Main study: 33 observers rating 30 representative images on interval emotion scales (rulers)
Large-scale application: 249,587 images from Flickr with computed emotion histograms
statistical_tests_used: Pearson correlation coefficient (r) for validating predictive model against observer judgments
Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Normalized RMSE (NRMS) for measuring interobserver agreement
Engeldrum normalization procedure for adjusting observer judgments to common scale
extraction_difficulties: No p-values reported for correlations; confidence intervals not provided
Activity factor correlation (0.86) weaker than heat (0.97) and weight (0.98) but no statistical test of significance difference
Intra-sample agreement calculations mentioned but detailed formulas not fully specified
Sample selection procedure complex (stratified sampling, representative coverage); exact sampling strategy not fully formalized
Figure 6 shows all observer judgments but individual statistical tests not reported; aggregate statistics only
methodological_notes: Predictive model based on equations (1)-(5) relating RGB values to three emotion factors via CIELAB transformation
Interval scaling method used in main study (observer positions samples on ruler) differs from pilot study category scaling (5 equal intervals)
Web-based studies limit control over viewing conditions; authors acknowledge as limitation
Interobserver agreement better for heat and weight than activity, suggesting these factors more intuitive
